metaDescription: Five string trimmers under $150 from BLACK+DECKER, WORX and Greenworks, including combo kits, compared on voltage, battery inclusion and edging features.
expertTake: The BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX kit is the best straight trimmer here because it includes the battery and charger and has a transmission built for torque. The Greenworks 40V trimmer and blower combo is the value pick if you also need a blower. Skip the 20V WORX units if your lawn has thick growth, since they are built for light edging. Check the live price and kit contents before ordering.
introParagraphs: At this ceiling you can buy a complete battery system from a major brand instead of a bare tool or an unnamed import. The tradeoffs shift to platform choice, whether a blower comes along and how much torque you really need. A complete kit is the first thing to look for.

A combo kit looks like a bargain, but only if you want both tools. Prices move and the $150 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so confirm the live number before buying. Treat the cap as a ceiling, not a target.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX 13-Inch Trimmer Edger Kit
products.description:
This is the complete-kit version of the 40V MAX trimmer, with the battery and charger in the box. The battery has a state-of-charge indicator so you can see how much runtime is left, which is surprisingly helpful in a cordless tool. A high-torque power drive transmission boosts the cutting strength at the head, and the 13-inch swath is wide for a battery trimmer.

The tool converts from trimming to edging in seconds, so one machine handles the lawn border and the sidewalk strip. Compared with the bare-tool listings that sit at lower prices, the real cost is easier to read here. Compared with the WORX 40V it has a longer-established battery platform and a clear kit.

The 40V MAX packs are shared across a range of the maker's outdoor tools, which lowers the cost of adding a hedge trimmer or blower later. Store the battery indoors and watch the indicator before long jobs. In year-three ownership, the battery is the part most likely to need replacing, so note the model number now. Wear eye protection and long trousers, since the 40V head throws stones and sticks with real force.
products.bestFor: A complete 40V trimmer without hunting for a battery.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12-Inch Trimmer and 390 CFM Blower Combo
products.description:
Greenworks bundles a 12-inch auto-feed trimmer with a 390 CFM, 110 MPH blower and a 2.0Ah battery. The trimmer uses .065-inch line and is described as slicing through weeds up to an inch thick along fences, while the blower clears wet leaves and debris from concrete. One battery runs both tools.

That sharing is the value: you carry one pack and finish a full cleanup. The tradeoff is that the single 2Ah battery must serve two jobs, so runtime is limited. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER kit, you get a blower instead of a more powerful trimmer.

It makes sense for a small yard where you trim edges and then blow clippings off the path. Plan the job so you trim first and blow afterward, otherwise clippings land on a clean path. A spare battery is the best upgrade, since two tools on one pack empties it faster than either alone. Rinse nothing near the motor housing.
products.bestFor: Small yards that need both trimming and blowing.

products.name: WORX WG183 40V 13-Inch Cordless String Trimmer
products.description:
The WORX WG183 emphasizes light weight and maneuverability, with a dual-exit cutting head that feeds two lines for better cutting efficiency. An automatic-feed spool system advances line without bumping. The streamlined design aims to reduce fatigue over a long session.

Check whether the listing includes a battery, as this brand often sells tools and batteries separately. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER kit, it is lighter but the cost picture depends on the pack. Against the 20V WORX models, it has more power.

It suits users who value handling over raw torque. Because the head feeds two lines, line use runs higher than a single-line head, so keep spare spool lines on hand. The light build makes it comfortable, though a light shaft flexes more in thick grass. Check the listing for a battery before you order.

products.name: WORX WG928 20V Trimmer and 360 CFM Blower Kit
products.description:
WORX pairs a 12-inch trimmer-edger with a 360 CFM leaf blower in a two-tool kit. The trimmer converts to an edger by pivoting the head, and a command feed system gives fresh line on demand with a button press. Both tools share the 20V PowerShare battery platform.

The combo is the cheapest way here to equip a small yard with two tools. Compared with the Greenworks combo it has a lower-voltage platform and a slightly weaker blower, but the PowerShare packs fit a wide range of WORX products.

Trim first, blow after, and swap the pack when one runs down. The combo suits a person who wants one purchase to cover the whole weekend chore. Charge the battery fully before starting and expect to take a short break between the trimming and blowing stages. Keep the blower nozzle clean of wet leaf paste.

products.name: WORX WG163 20V 12-Inch 2-in-1 Trimmer Edger
products.description:
The WG163 is a 12-inch trimmer that converts to an edger. The head tilts 90 degrees for slopes and for edging, and a push-button command feed gives instant line.

It is the simplest and cheapest WORX tool here. Compared with the combo, it has no blower.

Use it for light work. Tilt the head to follow the curve of a path, and tap the feed button only when the line is short. Check the battery listing, as WORX sells tools without packs. It is a good second tool to a mower owner who already has PowerShare batteries. Treat it as an edging specialist.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX kit includes its battery and charger. WORX and Greenworks often sell tools and batteries separately. Count the full cost before comparing prices, because a missing battery can double the bill. For comparison, a 20V tool with a 2Ah pack holds a fraction of the energy of a 40V pack of larger capacity. Write the model numbers down before you buy. Do the sums before ordering.

The BLACK+DECKER power drive adds torque at the head, which helps in thick grass. Light 20V units rely on a direct drive and stall sooner. If your lawn has tall growth, a transmission is worth more than higher RPM. Test the trimmer on your toughest patch if you can, because transmissions only show their value under load. Write the model numbers down before you buy. Heavy grass is where it shows.

The Greenworks and WORX combos include a blower. A blower is useful if you also clear paths, but one battery must power both tools. Buy a second pack if you plan to use both for long. If you already own a blower, a trimmer-only purchase is more efficient. Write the model numbers down before you buy. Choose what you will use.

40V is stronger than 20V and shares packs with more tools. A 20V PowerShare pack, though, works across a wide WORX range. Think about what other tools you will add. Check the charger time too, since a slow charger leaves you waiting a few hours. Write the model numbers down before you buy. Plan a charging schedule.

The WG163 tilts its head 90 degrees and the BLACK+DECKER converts quickly. Edging wears line quickly, so keep spare spools. Replacement line is cheap, but the right diameter matters. Write the model numbers down before you buy. Order extra spools.

The WORX WG183 promotes an ultra-light design. Weight matters over 30 minutes. Try a few and note the balance point. If you share the tool with a family member, adjustable grips are a bonus. Write the model numbers down before you buy. Comfort counts.

howToChoose.intro: Match the tool to the actual job, then check the box contents.
Tiers are relative and assume you buy a complete working kit.

cards.label: 20V
cards.text: The WORX WG163 and WG928 are lighter and cheaper but have limited torque. They are best for small lawns and tidy edges.

cards.label: 40V
cards.text: The BLACK+DECKER, Greenworks and WORX WG183 cut thicker growth and run longer. They share batteries with larger tools and are easier to expand.

howToChoose.note: Choose 40V if growth is thick. Many owners pick 20V for the shed tool and 40V for the weekend job.

howToChoose.intro: Decide how many tools you need before you pick a platform.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: 40V, a battery indicator and a spare pack. Add a second battery if you can.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX is the best fit. It also has a battery state indicator, which makes planning easier.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have over half an acre. Look at 56V or gas. A gas or 56V machine has the torque for that work. Weigh the extra pounds against the extra torque.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small lawn. The WORX WG163 is enough. Use the savings for line and a spare pack.
